## Overview

The purpose of the proposal is to get you to commit to an idea and think through what your final project will look like before you start building it. You will be choosing one of two tracks (see the [Project Description](/project/project-description.qmd)):

-   **Shiny app** --- an interactive tool that lets a user explore a data set and come away having learned something.
-   **Report** --- a polished written report, authored in Quarto, built around at least one well-crafted visualization.

Either way, the core questions are the same: What do you want your audience to learn? What data will get them there? And what will they see? Answer each of the four steps below in a paragraph or two. Short and specific beats long and vague---this is a plan, not a finished product, and it is fine if things change once you start working with the data.

::: {.callout-note}
If you are working in a group (up to three students), submit **one proposal** with everyone's names at the top and include a short note on how you plan to divide the work. See the [Project Description](/project/project-description.qmd) for the group policy.
:::

## Step 1: Your question and your track (25 pts.)

*What question or theme do you want your audience to explore, and which track are you choosing? Tell us why that track is the right fit for your question.*

*Then find a few examples that you would like your project to resemble and link to them:*

-   ***App track:*** *Browse the Shiny [gallery](https://shiny.posit.co/r/gallery/) and look back at the apps we built in [Shiny Basics](/modules/module-5.1.qmd) and [Advanced Shiny](/modules/module-5.2.qmd). Which **layouts** appeal to you most, and why?*
-   ***Report track:*** *Find one or two pieces of data journalism or policy reports (e.g., from [Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/), [Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/), or a newspaper's graphics desk) that do what you want to do. What do you like about how they combine writing and visuals?*

## Step 2: The data (25 pts.)

*What data sets will you use? These could be data sets that we have used in the course or other sources (see the [Datasets](/project/project-datasets.qmd) page for ideas), but they should be comprehensive and convenient to work with---you will not have time for original data collection. Be specific: name the source, the key variables or indicators, the units of observation (countries, states, years...) and the time span. If you plan to merge data sets, say how they will be joined.*

## Step 3: The visualization (25 pts.)

*What type of visualization will you build? This could be a line chart, scatter plot, bar chart, map, table or some combination, and it could include text elements as well. How will your visualization help your audience learn what you want them to learn? What should they notice when they look at it? A rough sketch (a photo of a drawing is fine) is welcome but not required.*

## Step 4: Interactivity or narrative (25 pts.)

***App track:*** *What will the user manipulate in your app? It could be a dropdown menu, a slider, radio buttons or some other control (see the list of [control widgets](https://shiny.posit.co/r/getstarted/shiny-basics/lesson3/)). When the user interacts with the control, what will change? How does that interaction help the user learn something they would not get from a static chart?*

***Report track:*** *How will your report be structured? Sketch an outline of the main sections and say where your visualization(s) will appear. What argument or story will the writing tell, and how will the visualization support it? Who is your intended audience?*

## Submission

*Write your answers in a Quarto document and submit your **unrendered QMD file** to Blackboard by 11:59 p.m. on `r advdate2(mon, 13)`. Groups submit once, with all members' names and the division-of-work note at the top.*
